title: Number systems and binary arithmetic

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Two’s complement, BCD and binary addition, with the working shown.

blocks.heading: Two’s complement and BCD
blocks.text: In an 8-bit two’s complement integer the most significant bit has the place value -128 and the other seven bits have their usual positive place values, 64 down to 1. So 1111 0110 is -128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 4 + 2, which is -10. Binary Coded Decimal is different: it stores each denary digit as its own 4-bit group, so denary 47 in BCD is 0100 0111.

blocks.heading: Adding in binary
blocks.text: Binary addition works column by column from the right. Zero and zero give 0; zero and one give 1; one and one give 0 with 1 carried to the next column; one, one and a carry give 1 with 1 carried. Overflow occurs when the result needs more bits than the register holds.

blocks.heading: Worked example
blocks.text: Add the unsigned 8-bit values 0010 1101 (45) and 0001 0111 (23). Working from the right, the columns give 0100 0100, with carries in five columns along the way. Check in denary: 45 + 23 = 68, and 0100 0100 is 64 + 4, which is 68. The result fits in 8 bits, so there is no overflow.
